Subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs / deployment topology

Hi Samir (and Elena),

Thanks again for carving out time today for the deep dive. Quick recap from our side and the agreed next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary of pain & goals:
- Production latency spikes during peak settlement windows (10x background load) causing timeouts for downstream fraud checks.
- Current infra: single-region GPU cluster, no KV-cache sharing across pods, per-request cold starts for models.
- Goal: 95th percentile generation latency <= 150ms for the primary risk-scoring model at 80 concurrent requests, with overall cost target to be within current monthly spend + 15%.

Technical highlights from today's call:
- Model family: you're running a transformer-based risk model (7B) tuned for short contexts (<=512 tokens); you mentioned a future evaluation for a 13B family.
- Target SLOs: 95th <=150ms, P99 <=300ms during peak windows; sustained throughput target ~800 reqs/min with 99.9% availability.
- Deployment topology discussed: multi-AZ routing + primary region dedicated GPU pool; hot KV prefix caching for common prefixes; automatic fallback to a quantized variant for cost spikes.
- Networking: pinning to a VPC with egress rules; we'll need a diagram of your current NAT/Transit Gateway config to validate MTU and TCP keepalive settings.

Action items (owners & timing):
1) Marissa: share SLO proposal + topology diagram (attached) and HubSpot deal link — today EOD.
2) Logan: provide quantization / model variant performance estimates and recommended GPU types for the 7B vs 13B options — by Fri 7/17.
3) Samir / Elena: share current infra diagram and a sample of perf data from peak window (CloudWatch / Prometheus) — by Thu 7/16.
4) Joint: schedule a small network review with your infra team if there are NAT/GW concerns — propose times next week.

Attachments: SLO_Proposal_v1.pdf (initial latency/cost tradeoffs), network_topology_diagram.png (our suggested starting topology).

Next meeting: you suggested Tue 7/20 for a hands-on perf estimation session; I'll send a calendar invite once I hear back on preferred times.

Thanks — feel free to correct anything I missed.

Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs / deployment topology

Thanks for the clear recap, Marissa. A couple of quick technical clarifications / preliminary notes from my side: 

- Model behavior: at <=512 tokens the 7B baseline with int8 quantization typically gives ~40-60% GPU memory reduction and about 1.6-1.9x throughput improvement vs fp16 on Ampere A10G; P95 can often be reduced by ~30-40ms with optimized kernels and fused attention.
- Warm KV cache: if FinTechCo can accept a short-lived cache (TTL 1-5 minutes) for session prefixes, we can eliminate a lot of repeated compute for similar requests during settlement bursts.
- Batching: request-level batching with latency SLO throttling (adaptive batching) will help us hit throughput targets while protecting P95. We'll need the per-request size distribution (median/95th token lengths).
- Quantized fallback: for cost control we can fallback to an 8-bit quantized 7B variant; quality regression tests are needed — I'll include initial eval numbers.

I'll attach a short table of GPU type recommendations and rough cost delta in the follow-up. For now, quick ask for Samir: can you share a 24-48 hour sample of request size distribution and a tight window sample from a peak day? That will help me size the dedicated pool.

Logan

Marissa / Logan,

Appreciate the recap and the quick turnaround. Confirming the notes look right from our side. A few clarifications: 

- Our model is a proprietary 7B variant running on GCP with custom tokenization; 95% of requests are <= 320 tokens, 95th token length is ~420 tokens during peak windows.
- Peak window: daily settlement batch around 02:00 UTC (US East) — that's when we see the 10x surge.
- We can provide a 48-hour sample export from our Prometheus cluster and a network diagram by EOD Thursday (7/16).

Next steps / asks from Redwood:
- Please include explicit P95/P99 numbers for both the fp16 baseline and the int8 quantized variant in the SLO proposal.
- Can you validate whether multi-AZ routing will add cross-AZ latency beyond our 150ms P95 target? If so, recommend an alternate topology.

We're excited to move forward with a pilot focused on the settlement window. Calendar invite for Tue 7/20 works for me — mornings ET preferred.
